importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is extreme — trailer-mounted, truck-mounted, tractor trolley, and three-wheeler configurations are visually distinct, as are MS vs FRP body types and 4-seater vs 14-seater scale. Buyers use the image to identify the correct product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Municipal tenders and institutional procurement explicitly specify seater count, body material, vehicle/mounting type, and waste system — buyers cannot shortlist or evaluate fit without these specs. Spec is the primary qualification gate before price comparison.

Price varies substantially across configurations — a 4-seater MS sludge-tank unit vs a 10-seater FRP bio-digester trailer carry very different price points. Indian institutional buyers are price-aggressive and compare across sellers within their spec tier; a visible price is essential for budget approval and shortlisting.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: The market is fragmented across regional fabricators with no nationally recognised brand that buyers search for by name; buyers search by spec and price, not manufacturer brand.
importance_ranking.reason: Institutional buyers (municipal corporations, government contractors) evaluate manufacturer status, government supply track record, ISO certification, and after-sales service capability during vendor selection — company credentials matter but are assessed after spec and price shortlisting.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Rental operators quote per day or per event, but all purchase transactions are per piece without exception. No buyer ever questions the unit for a fabricated vehicle assembly.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied — a mobile toilet van is always sold per piece regardless of seater count or configuration. No buyer confusion is possible.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Seater count is the primary SKU differentiator — non-interchangeable across buyer requirements and drives the largest price delta in the category (4-seater vs 12-seater represents a multi-fold price difference).

MS vs FRP body construction is non-interchangeable for most buyers (weight, corrosion resistance, and longevity differ substantially) and carries a significant price delta for equivalent seater configurations.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Municipal tenders and Swachh Bharat Mission guidelines routinely require separate male and female sections; sellers need this spec to confirm their unit layout meets the procurement requirement.

Fresh water tank and waste/sludge tank are separate components with independent capacities; buyers planning deployment duration and water resupply logistics require this spec, which is distinct from the waste Tank Capacity already in the list.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Seater count is non-interchangeable — a seller who fabricates only 4-seater units cannot supply a 10-seater requirement, and it is the primary determinant of price and physical scale.

Mounting configuration (trailer, tractor trolley, vehicle-mounted, portable) defines the deployment scenario and routes the RFQ to manufacturers who specialise in that configuration — a trailer-mounted fabricator cannot supply a three-wheeler-mounted unit.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Bio-digester, chemical tank, and sludge tank systems have different infrastructure requirements, compliance implications, and price points — sellers need this to confirm product eligibility and quote accurately, particularly for remote or rural deployments where pump-out infrastructure is unavailable.
